This slice does not boot vfkit, create a VM, run talosctl, or run kubectl against a live cluster.
This slice does not claim Kata workload readiness on Apple Silicon.
OpenTofu owns only the Cloudflare edge root, not the cluster fleet.
The control-plane access posture is Cloudflare Tunnel as L4 TCP passthrough to the apiserver VIP, preserving apiserver mTLS end-to-end.
Cloudflare Access must front k8s.oyatie.dev with least-privilege service-auth and optional human SSO/WARP policy.
Tunnel, Access, connector, and service-token secrets remain in Keychain/OpenBao or equivalent custody, never git.
Future live verification proves tokenless access is denied at Cloudflare Access before the apiserver and service-token access preserves client-certificate mTLS.
Future connector health evidence proves outbound-only cloudflared connectivity with no public inbound port.
future edge evidence: cloudflared /ready healthy, tunnel connection count, Access tokenless deny, and kubeconfig client cert success through local cloudflared access tcp
This slice does not run tofu plan/apply or modify Cloudflare resources.
This slice does not commit or inspect Cloudflare credentials, tunnel tokens, service-token material, talosconfig, kubeconfig, or private keys.
Cluster API initializes Talos, OCI, AWS, and Metal3 providers on the management control plane; it is not a kind-only bootstrap path.

Per-cell Argo CD owns app delivery by pull model after the CAPI/Talos cluster exists.
Kamaji is additive to ADR-0375 as the hosted-default CAPI control-plane provider; dedicated premium clusters continue through Talos control-plane providers.
A future live integration run records provider readiness, ClusterResourceSet render/apply evidence, Argo CD root Application health, and Kamaji TenantControlPlane reconciliation evidence.
The hosted and dedicated tiers share CAPI/Argo lifecycle semantics and differ only by control-plane placement.
